intent_signal: Commercial-investigation / pre-booking. Searchers (mostly Western, US/UK) are price-shopping a bundled 'arrive and just train' experience: they want to know what 'all-inclusive' actually covers (training + room + meals), what it costs per week/month, whether beginners are welcome, and which region/camp fits. They are comparing camps before committing, not yet booking a specific one.
common_ground: Standard inclusion stack: 2 sessions/day x 6 days/wk + on-site accommodation (dorm to private) + 2-3 meals/day + pool/gym access
Region framing (Phuket vs Chiang Mai vs Koh Samui vs Phetchabun) as a decision axis
Cost ranges quoted (often in USD/GBP) and 'is it worth it' justification
Mega-camps + aggregators dominate; most rank with brand authority or breadth, not depth of transparency

gap.description: The intent term is owned by Phuket mega-camps (Tiger, Bangtao) and booking aggregators (NOW Muay Thai, Tripaneer) — both of which are weak on exactly what the searcher most wants: a single, transparent, THB-native breakdown of what 'all-inclusive' really includes and what it costs. Aggregators deliberately HIDE prices to force booking; mega-camps scatter pricing across multiple pages and read as high-volume 'farang factories'. Nobody owning this term combines (a) honest THB package math (week/month/fighter), (b) a clear 'what's actually included vs what you arrange yourself' table, (c) a small family-run / female-led / open-air Chiang Mai angle that contrasts with the impersonal megacamp default, and (d) the 'Chiang Mai is cheaper and calmer than Phuket' value argument. That is a wide-open, low-competition (140/mo LOW) honesty-and-transparency angle.

weakness: Top organic results hide prices (aggregators) or fragment them across pages (mega-camps) — no clean THB bundle math
No competitor pairs 'all-inclusive' transparency with a small family-run / open-air Chiang Mai identity
Multi-discipline boot-camp / fight-outcome framing dominates; casual + beginner + 'just train and relax' is underserved with real numbers
Listicles/aggregators have thin per-camp E-E-A-T (generic bylines, promotional bias) — beatable by a real owner (Meaw) with first-hand authority
Phuket-centric; Chiang Mai 'all-inclusive' is barely contested at the head term despite being a cheaper, calmer alternative
recommended_angle: Build a transparent '#packages' section on the /stay-train pillar — NOT a standalone page yet. Reframe Wildcat's real THB week/month/fighter pricing as honest all-inclusive math: a plain table of what's actually included (training x2/day, gear loaned, garden/pool) vs what you arrange yourself (room + food nearby, since Wildcat is open-air and not a closed resort), positioned as the warm, family-run, female-led Chiang Mai alternative to impersonal Phuket mega-camps — and cheaper/calmer too. VERDICT: section of the pillar. At 140/mo LOW with the term split between megacamps and price-hiding aggregators, a transparent #packages section captures the comparison/price intent and strengthens the pillar's authority; only spin it into a dedicated page if Wildcat ever offers a truly bundled room+meals package (it currently does not — so a standalone 'all-inclusive' page would over-promise).
